I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model writes a tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You picked "it will eventually fix the bug". The agent keeps getting the same failing result, so more steps won't help. It needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is right. But your reasoning said the model runs the tools, and the program runs them. |
| q5 | correct | The result goes back as the model's next input, so the model can decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | You said the model goes by the tool's name. It actually reads the whole description: the name, what the tool does and its parameters. |

**Summary:** You have the core idea that the model writes a request and the program runs it, and that's an improvement on your first attempt. Two things to fix. An agent needs a stopping condition. And when you explain a tool-call count, say that the program runs the tools.

**Next step:** Write the description for `check_calendar`, with its name, purpose and parameters. Then trace one request through the loop, saying who does each step: the model or the program. Send it to me and I'll check it.
